{{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA AmeriCup]]}} {{MedalSilver|[[2013 FIBA Americas Championship|2013 Venezuela]]|}} }} '''John Michael Joseph Holland''' (born November 6, 1988) is an American-Puerto Rican professional [[basketball]] player for [[Santeros de Aguada]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] (BSN). A [[small forward]], he played college basketball for the [[Boston University Terriers men's basketball|Boston Terriers]] and represents the [[Puerto Rico national basketball team|Puerto Rican national team]]. ==High school career== Holland attended [[Fordham Preparatory School|Fordham Prep]] where he averaged 16 points, eight rebounds, eight assists and three steals, earning a McDonald's All-American nomination, a CHSAA All-Division naming and All-County honors from the Journal News. He also played for [[Saint Benedict's Preparatory School|Saint Benedict's Prep]] where he averaged 10 points, six rebounds, six assists, three steals and two blocks per game.{{cite web|url=http://www.goterriers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/holland_john00.html |title=Boston University bio |work=GoTerriers.com |access-date=December 21, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222132152/http://www.goterriers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/holland_john00.html |archive-date=December 22, 2015 }} ==College career== Holland played [[college basketball]] for [[Boston University Terriers men's basketball|Boston University]] where as a junior in [[2009–10 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2009–10]], he led the [[America East Conference]] in scoring with 19.2 points per game. He repeated as scoring champion in [[2010–11 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2010–11]] after again averaging 19.2 points. He was subsequently named [[America East Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year]] and led the Terriers to an NCAA Tournament berth.{{cite news|url=http://www.americaeast.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=205126024|title=John Holland Earns AP All-America Recognition in Men's Basketball|work=AmericaEast.com|date=March 29, 2011|access-date=September 10, 2011}} ==Professional career== ===European career (2011–2015)=== Holland went undrafted in the [[2011 NBA draft]]. On July 5, 2011, he signed with [[Chorale Roanne Basket]] of France for the 2011–12 season.{{cite news|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/87085/chorale-roanne-tabs-rookies-john-holland-and-rick-jackson.html|title=Chorale Roanne tabs rookies John Holland and Rick Jackson|work=Sportando.com|date=July 5, 2011|access-date=September 10, 2011}} In 28 games, he averaged 14.3 points, 4.7 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game.{{cite news|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/euro/players/john-holland-1.html|title=John Holland Europe Stats|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=April 11, 2016}} In July 2012, Holland joined the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] for the Orlando Summer League and the [[Miami Heat]] for the Las Vegas Summer League. On August 5, 2012, he signed with [[CB Sevilla|Cajasol Sevilla]] of Spain for the 2012–13 season.{{cite news|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/94214/sevilla-officially-signs-john-holland.html|title=Sevilla officially signs John Holland|work=Sportando.com|date=August 5, 2012|access-date=August 5, 2012}} In 33 Liga ACB games, he averaged 10.4 points, 2.8 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 0.7 steals per game and in 12 Eurocup games, he averaged 10.1 points, 1.9 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 1.0 steals. In July 2013, Holland joined the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]]. On October 29, 2013, he signed with [[BCM Gravelines]] of France for the 2013–14 season.{{cite news|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/107518/john-holland-moves-to-gravelines-dunkerque.html|title=John Holland moves to Gravelines-Dunkerque|work=Sportando.com|date=October 29, 2013|access-date=October 29, 2013}} He played in 23 Pro A games averaging 10.9 points, 3.2 rebounds and 1.3 assists in 26.3 minutes and also appeared in 13 Eurocup games, averaging 9.9 points, 3.7 rebounds and 1.5 assists in 29.5 minutes.{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/140926_spurs_announce_training_camp_roster|title=Spurs Announce 2014-15 Training Camp Roster|work=NBA.com|date=September 26, 2014|access-date=September 26, 2014}} On September 26, 2014, Holland signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. However, he was later waived by the Spurs on October 13.{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/141013_spurs_waive_john_holland|title=Spurs Waive John Holland|work=NBA.com|date=October 13, 2014|access-date=October 13, 2014}} The next day, he signed with [[Beşiktaş men's basketball team|Beşiktaş]] of Turkey for the 2014–15 season.{{cite news|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/137615/besiktas-announces-john-holland.html|title=Besiktas announces John Holland|work=Sportando.com|date=October 14, 2014|access-date=October 14, web|url=http://canton.dleague.nba.com/news/john-holland-returns-charge/|title=John Holland Returns to Charge|work=NBA.com|date=December 9, 2016|access-date=December 9, 2016|archive-date=December 21, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161221170538/http://canton.dleague.nba.com/news/john-holland-returns-charge/|url-status=dead}} At the end of the season, he was named the D-League's Impact Player of the Year. After the end of the [[2016-17 NBA Development League season]], Holland signed with the [[Beijing Eastern Bucks]] of the [[National Basketball League (China)|Chinese National Basketball League]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/232261/john-holland-inks-with-beijing-eastern-ducks.html|title=John Holland inks with Beijing Eastern Ducks}} However, he left the Beijing before appearing in a single game for them. ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2017–2018)=== [[File:David Nwaba 2018.jpg|thumb|right|Holland (right) guards Cavaliers teammate [[David Nwaba]] during a scrimmage in 2018]] On September 8, 2017, Holland was signed to a [[two-way contract]] by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] of the NBA. Under the terms of the deal, he will split time between the Cavs and their G-League affiliate, the Canton Charge.{{cite news|title=Cavaliers Sign John Holland to Two-Way Contract |url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/holland-signing-170908|access-date=September 8, 2017|work=[[NBA.com]]|date=September 8, 2017}} Holland is the first player the Cavaliers have signed on such a deal. He would also play his first NBA regular season games during this contract after previously only playing in one playoff game for Boston. With the Cavaliers, Holland played 24 games and averaged 2.3 points per game. He went on to win the Eastern Conference championship with the Cavaliers, advancing to the [[2018 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]]. However, Cleveland, led by All-Star [[LeBron James]], were swept by the [[Golden State Warriors]]. Holland was waived by the Cavs on November 9, 2018.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/harrison-signing-181109|title=Cavaliers Sign Andrew Harrison to Two-Way On June 29, 2023, he announced that he would be parting ways with the club. ===Hapoel Tel Aviv (2023–2024)=== On July 27, 2023, he signed with [[Hapoel Tel Aviv B.C.|Hapoel Tel Aviv]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/john-holland-joins-hapoel-tel-aviv/|title=John Holland joins Hapoel Tel Aviv|last=|first=|date=July 27, 2023|website=|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=July 29, 2023 |last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }} ===Santeros de Aguada (2025–present)=== On January 2, 2025, Holland signed a contract with [[Santeros de Aguada]] until 2027. ==National team career== Holland is of Puerto Rican descent through his mother.
